small_guidance:
- The fused pool+sum kernel is fine but tiny (~5K programs); the conv_transpose dominates runtime. Tuning BLOCK_C/num_warps here will not move the needle — focus must shift to the conv.
- If keeping this kernel, try `num_warps=2` and reorder the triple static loop so the innermost axis is `ww` with contiguous W loads (already the case); also consider a 2D tile over (oh,ow) per program to amortize address math.
- Add `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` hints on the W-axis pointer to encourage vectorized loads.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the input×kernel outer product and atomically scattering into the output grid with stride=2, padding=2. This is the heavy op (output is 16×64×63×63×63 ≈ 260M elements) and the only path to large speedup.
- Better: fuse the entire pipeline by inverting the loop — iterate over output pool windows (6×6×6 at stride 6 in the post-conv grid, = 12×12×12 input-region with overlap) and compute conv_transpose contributions on the fly per output element, then max-reduce and sum across channels in registers. This avoids ever materializing the 260M-element conv output.
- Fold the conv bias into the kernel epilogue (added once per output position before max), and keep weights in `channels_last_3d` / `(IC, kD, kH, kW, OC)` layout so the GEMM-K dimension (IC×kD×kH×kW) is contiguous for coalesced loads.
